newsitem.title: DENMARK: U.N. opens new combined centre in Copenhagen.
newsitem.headline: U.N. opens new combined centre in Copenhagen.

text.p: The United Nations opened a new combined centre for several of its agencies in Copenhagen on Monday, and added a new purchasing office with an annual budget of 500 million Danish crowns ($85 million).

The new U.N. centre houses three of the world body's agencies -- IAPSO, the purchasing organ for the United Nations Development Programme, UNOPS, the office for project services and FAO/EASTFISH, a UN Food & Agricultural Organisation project, the Danish Foreign ministry said.
It said total U.N. staff in Copenhagen would be increased by 40 from just under the 600 presently employed.
New York-based UNOPS, which buys goods and services for development projects, opens a Copenhagen purchasing office with a 500 million crown budget and staff of 30.
UNDP and IAPSO are already operating in Copenhagen, as is its children's agency UNICEF and WHO, the World Health Organisation, which has its European regional headquarters in the Danish capital.
